verdicts.claim: limit200: searchHardware caps at LIMIT 200 ORDER BY Hardware_ID__c. On accounts with >200 Hardware records, a newly-created record (whose Hardware_ID__c is always non-null) is not returned by the post-create searchHardware call, so handleCreateHardware's .find(hw=>hw.Id===newHardwareId) returns undefined, leaving selectedHardware null and the Create Group button greyed out despite a success toast.
evidence: HardwareGroupController.cls:88-130 searchHardware: 'WHERE Account__c=:accountId ORDER BY Hardware_ID__c LIMIT 200'. Post-create call passes filters:{} (empty map), so the !isEmpty() branch is skipped and no status/serial/model clause is added -> queries the full account domain.

HardwareGroupController.cls:138-215,655-672 createHardwareRecord ALWAYS sets Hardware_ID__c (generateHardwareId()='HW'+count.leftPad(6) at line 151, OR Cross-Platform user override at lines 187-190) -> new record's Hardware_ID__c is NEVER null.

hardwareGroupManager.js:769-784: createdHardware = newHardwareRecords.find(hw=>hw.Id===newHardwareId); the if(createdHardware) block that sets selectedHardware is skipped when find()===undefined; showToast('Success') at line 786 fires unconditionally.

hardwareGroupManager.js:145-152 + 258-260: create-mode canFinish requires selectedHardware!==null; with it null, canFinishDisabled=true => 'Create Group' button greyed out. Matches all three reported symptoms.
Live FortraUAT: account 001WC00000XiZP4YAN has 236 Hardware records (COUNT(Id)=236 verified).

Live FortraUAT DECISIVE test: SELECT Hardware_ID__c FROM Hardware__c WHERE Account__c='001WC00000XiZP4YAN' ORDER BY Hardware_ID__c LIMIT 200 returns 200 rows with ZERO non-null Hardware_ID__c. 228 null-ID records occupy positions 1-228 (Salesforce NULLS FIRST), and the only 8 non-null IDs sit at positions 229-236 -- entirely past the LIMIT 200 cutoff.

Those 8 non-null IDs (HW000033/032/031/030, 123456, 123, 12123, HW000013) ARE the orphan Quoting records created via this LWC and never grouped; 6 were created by reporter German Wren on 2026-06-16/17 (CreatedBy + CreatedDate verified) -- live victims of this exact bug.

Simulation: global HW% count=34 -> generateHardwareId()=HW000035, sorts to position 237 (excluded). Even the lowest-possible non-null text values ('aaa'=232, '000001'=229) land past 200 because 228 nulls precede ALL non-null text under NULLS-FIRST -> exclusion is robust to any new ID value.
verdicts.strongestCounterargument: The staged-evidence framing ("235 records sort before HW000033", "229 before 123") implies the cutoff is driven by the new value sorting past 200 relative to other real Hardware IDs. Live data shows the actual dominant mechanism is different: 228 of the 236 records have a NULL Hardware_ID__c and, under Salesforce's default NULLS-FIRST ASC ordering, those nulls monopolize positions 1-228, pushing all 8 non-null IDs into the 229-236 band. So the claim's conclusion is right but its stated mechanism understates that the true driver is the nulls-first window, not value-vs-value ordering. A secondary co-failure also exists: the post-create searchHardware is @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true) called imperatively, so even on a sub-200 account a stale Lightning cache could omit the just-inserted row -- meaning LIMIT 200 is the primary but not the only way find() can return undefined. Neither point refutes limit200 as the primary, deterministic root cause on this account.
verdicts.notes: CONFIRMED and DETERMINISTIC on 001WC00000XiZP4YAN. Direct empirical proof: the exact production LIMIT 200 query returns 0 non-null Hardware_ID__c rows; every newly-created record has a non-null Hardware_ID__c, so find() is guaranteed undefined. The 8 live orphan Quoting records (positions 229-236, 6 by the reporter) are the smoking gun. Fix-owner refinement: root cause is sort-order + LIMIT combined with 228 null-ID records, not value math. Robust fixes: query the new record by Id directly after insert, have createHardwareRecord return the full record, or remove/raise the LIMIT and drop cacheable=true on the post-create read. verdicts.claim: SECONDARY TRIGGER: searchHardware is @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true); imperative calls are client-cached by signature+args, so a repeated searchHardware(accountId,{}) in the same session can return a stale result missing a just-created record, breaking .find() even on small accounts — assess if real and whether the FIRST create is affected.
evidence: HardwareGroupController.cls:88 — `@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true) public static List<Hardware__c> searchHardware(...)`: the method IS cacheable, so imperative calls route through the Lightning storable-action client cache (keyed by controller+method+serialized args, with TTL). Mechanism is real in principle.

hardwareGroupManager.js:769 — the post-create call is `searchHardware({accountId, filters: {}})`, and grep shows this is the ONLY searchHardware call in the create-group repro path. With no prior identical-signature call, the FIRST create's call is a cache MISS -> server hit -> reflects the insert. The cache cannot cause the first-create failure.

hardwareGroupManager.js:438 — the only other caller `handleSearchHardware` passes `this.searchFilters` = {status:'',category:'',environment:'',serialNumber:'',model:''} (5 empty-string keys), which serializes to a DIFFERENT cache key than `{}`. So even a prior manual search would not prime/hit the line-769 signature.

Live data: `SELECT COUNT(Id) FROM Hardware__c WHERE Account__c='001WC00000XiZP4YAN'` = 236; null Hardware_ID__c = 228, non-null = 8. Under `ORDER BY Hardware_ID__c ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 200` (HardwareGroupController.cls:122-123), a new HW0000NN record ranks ~237 (228 nulls + 8 lower non-null IDs + 1) — outside the 200-row window on EVERY create. This LIMIT truncation is the deterministic, cache-independent cause of the .find()==undefined symptom.

hardwareGroupManager.js:1040-1043 + quoteLineFlexPanel.js:345 — refreshApex only targets wiredGroupsResult (not the imperative searchHardware cache); the host does window.location.reload() on group-create success, wiping the client cache between groups. So a stale-cache searchHardware can only occur for a 2nd+ create within ONE uninterrupted modal session — a narrow, non-default path, not the reported repro.

createHardwareRecord (cls:138) and searchHardware are two separate client->server requests / Apex transactions; the client cache has no DML-awareness and won't auto-invalidate after the insert — which keeps the stale-replay mechanism plausible for repeated same-key calls, but only on the 2nd+ create.
verdicts.strongestCounterargument: The strongest case FOR treating it as a genuine contributing trigger: the mechanism is undeniably real — searchHardware IS cacheable (cls:88), the post-create call uses a stable `(accountId, {})` key, there is no refreshApex/cache-bust on that path, and Apex DML in a separate transaction does not invalidate the client action cache. So if a tester creates two hardware records back-to-back in a single modal session (plausible during QA), the 2nd searchHardware(accountId,{}) can legitimately replay the 1st pre-insert result and drop the 2nd record from .find() even on a tiny account — exactly the described stale-cache failure, with no LIMIT involvement. This makes 'cache as secondary trigger' defensible rather than fully refuted.
verdicts.notes: Net assessment: PARTIAL. (1) The mechanism is technically correct and searchHardware is in fact cacheable=true, so the claim is not wrong. (2) But it does NOT explain the reported, first-create symptom and does NOT affect the FIRST create: that call is a cache miss and the failure is caused deterministically by `ORDER BY Hardware_ID__c ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 200` placing the new (non-null-ID) record at rank ~237 of 236, outside the window — true for this 236-row account on every create, zero cache needed. (3) The cache can only contribute on a 2nd+ create within one uninterrupted modal session (different signature from handleSearchHardware's searchFilters, and host page-reload wipes it between groups), making it at most a minor edge-case secondary trigger, not the primary cause. Recommended fixes target the real cause: remove/raise LIMIT 200 and order so new records surface (or, simplest, construct the selected-hardware object from createHardwareRecord's return + form data instead of re-querying). If they additionally want to harden against the 2nd-create cache edge, either make searchHardware non-cacheable for this imperative use or stop re-querying entirely.

verdicts.strongestCounterargument: The single strongest alternative was the Partition__c insert: it shares the same try-block as the Hardware insert (HardwareGroupController.cls:215-241), so a Partition failure WOULD throw, roll back the Hardware insert, and surface an error toast instead of success. If that were happening, no record would persist and the symptom could superficially look similar. However, this is refuted directly: the repro Hardware records AND their P1 partitions both exist in the org, the toast shown is 'success' (not error), and the symptom is specifically 'record not in list + button greyed' rather than an error toast. A secondary counterargument is that the QuoteLineGroup VR Hardware_Groups_Must_Have_Hardware could block the final Create Group save - but that VR can only fire after the button is enabled and clicked, whereas the reported bug is the button never becoming clickable, so the VR is downstream of the defect and not its cause.
verdicts.notes: Alternative-cause sweep is fully refuted; the find/LIMIT-200 mechanism is the sole cause and is corroborated both statically (code paths) and empirically (live org data). Two genuine but SEPARATE secondary issues exist and should not be conflated with the root cause: (1) the success toast at hardwareGroupManager.js:786 fires unconditionally even when find() returns undefined (cosmetic mis-signal that masks the bug); (2) nulls in Hardware_ID__c sort first under ORDER BY Hardware_ID__c ASC (the first-200 window contained null IDs, 'first id: None'), which consumes window slots and can make the cutoff bite even on accounts nearer the 200 boundary. Both are facets of the same find/LIMIT design flaw, not alternative root causes. Fix should target searchHardware (query the new record by Id directly, or remove/raise the LIMIT and the unconditional toast), not any VR/trigger/FLS/dup-rule. synthesis.rootCauseStatement: SC-3423 is a client/server read-after-write design flaw in the hardwareGroupManager LWC + HardwareGroupController Apex. After createHardwareRecord inserts a new Hardware__c (always with a non-null Hardware_ID__c — generateHardwareId() 'HW'+padded count, or the Cross-Platform user override), handleCreateHardware re-derives the just-created record by calling searchHardware({accountId, filters:{}}) and doing newHardwareRecords.find(hw => hw.Id === newHardwareId). searchHardware runs 'WHERE Account__c=:accountId ORDER BY Hardware_ID__c LIMIT 200'. On any account with >200 Hardware rows, the new record falls outside that 200-row window, so find() returns undefined; the entire if(createdHardware){…} block (which is the ONLY place selectedHardware is set in this path) is skipped, yet showToast('Success') fires unconditionally and unguarded afterward. With selectedHardware still null and assignHardwareNow=true, canFinish requires selectedHardware!==null, so canFinishDisabled=true keeps the 'Create Group' button greyed — exactly the three reported symptoms (success toast, record not in list, button greyed). The dominant truncation driver on the reporter's account 001WC00000XiZP4YAN (236 rows) is that 228/236 Hardware_ID__c are NULL and SOQL's default NULLS-FIRST ASC ordering monopolizes positions 1-228, so the production LIMIT-200 window literally contains ZERO non-null IDs (live-verified) — the new record can never appear regardless of its value. A real but secondary contributor is @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true) on searchHardware, which can serve a stale client cache on a 2nd+ create within one modal session; it does NOT cause the first-create repro. The same LIMIT 200 also truncates getUnassignedHardware, which populates the initial 'Available Hardware' list, so larger accounts can't even see/select existing hardware.

fixOptions.summary: Stop re-querying: build the selected-hardware object from createHardwareRecord's return + the form data (or have createHardwareRecord return the full Hardware__c SObject)
fixOptions.change: Change createHardwareRecord to 'return newHardware;' (full SObject with the fields searchHardware selects) instead of 'return newHardware.Id;'. In handleCreateHardware, set this.selectedHardware/this.hardwareRecords directly from that returned record (or assemble from hardwareData + newHardwareId), then fetchHardwareAttributes(createdHardware.Id). Delete the post-create searchHardware re-query and the find().
fixOptions.pros: Eliminates the read-after-write entirely; LIMIT-200, ORDER BY, NULLS-FIRST, and cacheable-stale-cache all become irrelevant on the create path. No extra SOQL. Minimal, fully deterministic, no governor/sharing surprises. Survives accounts of any size.
fixOptions.cons: Requires the Apex return type/signature change (Id->Hardware__c) plus an Apex test update; both callers of the returned value must be checked. Slightly more LWC mapping code. Newly inserted record won't carry any DB-default/trigger-computed fields unless re-queried by Id — mitigate by re-selecting the inserted row by Id (see option b) before returning.

fixOptions.summary: Query the new record by Id (and/or remove/raise LIMIT) instead of relying on the 200-row account window
fixOptions.change: Either (b1) add a small Apex method getHardwareById(Id) that selects the single row by Id and call it post-create; or (b2) in createHardwareRecord, after insert, re-select the row by Id and return the full SObject; or (b3) raise/remove the LIMIT 200 in searchHardware and order so new records surface (e.g. ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC, or NULLS LAST). Prefer by-Id selection for the create path.
fixOptions.pros: By-Id selection is O(1), deterministic, immune to ordering/limit/null distribution. Pairs naturally with option (a). If LIMIT is also raised on searchHardware it fixes manual-search truncation too.
fixOptions.cons: Raising/removing LIMIT 200 on searchHardware risks larger result sets / governor and LWC datatable perf on 1000+ row accounts — should be bounded (e.g. LIMIT 2000) and ideally paginated/server-filtered, not unbounded. Adds one Apex method/round-trip if using getHardwareById.

fixOptions.summary: Remove cacheable from searchHardware (or bypass cache) for the post-create read
fixOptions.change: Either drop @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true) on searchHardware (make it @AuraEnabled), or keep it cacheable for read paths but use a non-cacheable method for the post-create lookup, or call refreshApex/notifyRecordUpdateAvailable. If option (a)/(b) removes the post-create searchHardware call, this becomes moot for the create path.
fixOptions.pros: Closes the 2nd+-create stale-cache edge case. Cheap if done as a separate non-cacheable read method.
fixOptions.cons: Making searchHardware non-cacheable removes caching benefit for legitimate repeated manual searches (minor perf). Does NOT by itself fix the primary LIMIT-200 cause (the record is genuinely absent from a fresh query). Only meaningful AFTER the LIMIT/find issue is fixed.

fixOptions.summary: Make the success toast / flow conditional so a failed create is not silently reported as success
fixOptions.change: In handleCreateHardware, only showToast('Success') inside the createdHardware branch; in the else branch showToast('Warning'/'Error','Hardware created but could not be selected…') and keep showCreateHardware open / do not claim success. Optionally guard against the empty if-block masking. Even after (a)/(b), keep a guard so any future read-miss surfaces an error rather than a false success.
fixOptions.pros: Defense-in-depth: prevents the most damaging symptom (silent failure that masks the bug and leaves orphans). Trivial change. Improves diagnosability for any residual edge case.
fixOptions.cons: Cosmetic only — does not fix the root cause by itself; must be combined with (a)/(b). Slight risk of false-negative toast if the record genuinely exists but a transient read failed (acceptable).

fixOptions.summary: Fix getUnassignedHardware LIMIT 200 truncation of the initial Available Hardware list
fixOptions.change: Apply the same treatment to getUnassignedHardware (lines 376-411): raise/remove the bounded LIMIT, add server-side search/pagination, and/or order so relevant rows surface (and consider NULLS handling on Hardware_ID__c). Ensure assigned-exclusion still works.
fixOptions.pros: Fixes the parallel defect where existing hardware beyond row 200 is invisible/unselectable on large accounts — restores ability to assign existing hardware, not just newly created. Same root design flaw, so fixing both prevents a 'whack-a-mole' re-report.
fixOptions.cons: Unbounded queries on 1000+ row accounts (top=1172) risk LWC datatable perf and governor pressure; really needs pagination/server filtering to be safe, which is more work. Should bound LIMIT and add search rather than remove the cap entirely.

synthesis.recommendedFix: Primary: option (a) + (b2) together — change createHardwareRecord to re-select the inserted row by Id and return the full Hardware__c SObject, and in the LWC set selectedHardware/hardwareRecords directly from that return (deleting the post-create searchHardware re-query and find()). This eliminates the read-after-write that the whole bug depends on, is O(1), and is structurally immune to LIMIT 200, ORDER BY, NULLS-FIRST, and the cacheable stale cache — it works on accounts of any size (including the 1172-row account). Add option (d) as cheap defense-in-depth so the success toast is gated on actually having a selected record, ensuring no future read-miss is ever silently reported as success. Treat option (e) (getUnassignedHardware truncation) as a REQUIRED companion fix so existing hardware beyond row 200 is selectable — but implement it as a bounded/paginated server-side search (LIMIT raised to e.g. 2000 + filter), NOT an unbounded query, given the 1172-row account. Option (c) becomes unnecessary on the create path once (a)/(b) remove the post-create searchHardware call; only drop cacheable if searchHardware is still used for any read-after-write. Rationale: minimal blast radius (no VR/trigger/sharing/FLS involved — altcause sweep REFUTED those), fixes the deterministic primary cause and the silent-failure masking, and durably covers every account size rather than just raising a limit that a 1000+ row account would blow past again.

synthesis.dataCleanup: The 26 Status='Quoting' orphan Hardware__c records are interim artifacts of the create-hardware flow, but they are NOT uniformly products of THIS bug. Verified split: 6 of the 26 ARE referenced by a QuoteLineGroup (HW000012/16/22/26/27/28) and sit on small (<200-row) accounts where find() succeeds — these are LEGITIMATELY grouped, in-use, and MUST NOT be deleted. The remaining ~20 are ungrouped orphans; of those, German Wren's 6 on 001WC00000XiZP4YAN (HW000030-33, '123', '123456', created 2026-06-16/17) plus Liam's repro HW000034 (2026-06-18) are confirmed victims of this >200-row bug (ranks 230-236, all past the LIMIT-200 cutoff, none grouped). Other small-account orphans (e.g. Marc DeBrey's HW000001-005 on an 8-record account, HW000023 on a 21-record account) are below 200 and therefore from a DIFFERENT cause (abandoned flow / deleted group), so do not attribute them to SC-3423. Recommended cleanup: (1) do NOT mass-delete by Status='Quoting'; (2) target only ungrouped Quoting records (no QuoteLineGroup.Hardware__c reference) AND not referenced by any Order/Asset, after owner sign-off — delete each Hardware and its child Partition (e.g. HW######-P1) together to avoid orphan partitions; (3) at minimum, delete/relabel the confirmed German Wren + Liam repro records on 001WC00000XiZP4YAN once the fix is verified, since they will otherwise keep occupying non-null-ID slots; (4) consider a follow-up scheduled cleanup of Quoting hardware older than N days that is never grouped. Get explicit authorization before any UAT DML (read-only inspection only so far).
